chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) - about a man who passes through some of the cities, and he has a house in that city, but that city is not his homeland: does he complete his prayer or shorten it? He said, 'He shortens the prayer, and the agricultural estates are like that; if he passes through them.'
ai.seo_question: Does a person shorten their prayer if they have a house in a city they are just passing through, even if it is not their hometown?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between permanent residence (watan) and secondary dwellings in determining travel status (safar) for prayer shortening. It establishes that possessing a home in a city does not negate traveler status if it is not one's primary homeland, extending this logic to agricultural estates to emphasize the principle of temporary versus permanent habitation.
